chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from some of his men, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him: 'Does the earth remain without an Imam?' He replied: 'No.'

key_terms.إِمَام: Imam, the divinely appointed leader and proof of God on earth
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: The earth, referring to the inhabited world or the realm of divine authority

ai.seo_question: Does the earth ever remain without an Imam according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* anchors the Shia doctrine of *Istidrar al-Imamah* (the continuity of Imamate), asserting that God never leaves the earth without a *Hujjah* (proof) to guide humanity. The Imam’s definitive 'No' underscores the metaphysical necessity of the Imam for the stability of the cosmos, a concept central to both Twelver and Ismaili theology regarding the unseen presence of the Imam during the Major Occultation.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (5) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from some of his companions from Ahmad bin Mihran from Muhammad bin Ali that al-Husayn bin Abul Ala’ had asked Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as):
“Is the world left without an imam?” He replied: “No, it is not.”
